title: POC scoping - Integration planning with Lyra Systems
summary: AE + SE scoped a 6-week POC for Lyra Systems focused on integrating Redwood API via OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs. Key success criteria: latency < 200ms median for chat flows, cost per 1k tokens under target, accurate structured JSON outputs for downstream ingestion. Plan includes baseline benchmarks, an initial pilot on hosted Redwood API, followed by evaluation on Dedicated if throughput or data isolation requirements emerge.
next_steps: Nora to send POC proposal + pricing (hosted vs dedicated) by 2026-12-09
Diego to share sample SDK snippets (Python/Node) and OpenAI-compatible endpoint docs by 2026-12-08
Lyra to provide 5 representative prompt templates and dataset sample for benchmark by 2026-12-10
Schedule benchmark run (week of 2026-12-14) and follow-up review call week of 2026-12-21
action_items: Nora Chen: prepare POC statement of work + pricing options (due 2026-12-09)
Diego Ruiz: provide SDK examples, function-calling examples, and structured output examples (due 2026-12-08)
Amira Patel: share example prompts, expected JSON schema, and 1k-row sample dataset (due 2026-12-10)
Sofia Reyes: provide network constraints and any VPC/KMS requirements (due 2026-12-10)
transcript:
[00:00] Nora Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Nora from Redwood, AE on this engagement. We also have Diego, our solutions engineer. Can you all introduce?
[00:07] Amira Patel: Hi, Amira here, CTO at Lyra. We've been evaluating a few inference options for our in-product assistant.
[00:13] Ben Zhou: Ben, ML engineering. I'll own the benchmark and integration work on our side.
[00:17] Sofia Reyes: Sofia, infra. I'm here for network and security questions.
[00:22] Diego Ruiz: Great to meet you all. Quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, then deep dive into integration — SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling and structured outputs.
[00:35] Amira: Sounds good. High level: we want to add a contextual assistant into our analytics UI, needs real-time-ish chat, and also a structured extraction endpoint to feed into our pipelines.
[00:44] Nora: Perfect. Can you share top success metrics? latency, cost, quality?
[00:50] Amira: Latency is big. We want median < 200ms token generation for short chats (under 512 tokens). For longer runs it's ok to be higher. Cost target is, roughly, under $0.50 per 1k tokens equivalent — we can vary if quality is significantly better. Lastly, structured output accuracy at at least 92% for key fields.
[01:10] Diego: Thanks. That's helpful. On workload sizing, what's your expected RPS and concurrency?
[01:15] Ben: For phase 1 POC, about 50 concurrent users during peak — say 25 rps average, spikes up to 60 rps. Typical request size around 200-400 tokens in and 50-150 tokens out.
[01:30] Diego: Okay that maps to hosted API for initial POC. If needed we can propose dedicated capacity for predictable throughput — but we'll run baseline benchmarks first.
[01:40] Sofia: On data residency, we need logs to be retained for 30 days and KMS-managed keys if we go private. Also SSO for the console.
[01:48] Nora: We support KMS integrations and SSO (SAML), and audit logs with retention options — we'll include those in the security docs.
[01:55] Amira: Good. For integration we prefer OpenAI-compatible endpoints so we can reuse some of our existing client code. Any caveats?
[02:02] Diego: Redwood exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints and native SDKs. Function calling and structured output are supported; we have examples for model responses that emit strict JSON per schema. One caveat: fallback models sometimes alter formatting — we'll demo a strict output enforcement pattern during benchmarks.
[02:20] Ben: For the function-calling, do you support tool invocation patterns similar to OpenAI's function calling?
[02:24] Diego: Yes, very similar. You can define functions with JSON schemas, call them, and receive typed responses. We also support streaming with incremental function-calling hooks so you can start handling tokens while the model is generating.
[02:36] Amira: Great. Will we need to change our prompt templates?
[02:39] Ben: We have some prompt engineering already but will share canonical templates. We want Redwood to run our prompts unchanged for baseline, then we'll iterate.
[02:46] Diego: For SDKs, we have Python and Node first-class SDKs; we can also support curl/OpenAI-compatible clients. I'll drop sample snippets that show: 1) calling the chat endpoint, 2) registering a function with schema, 3) streaming and structured-output validation.
[03:02] Nora: On benchmarks: we'll run baseline on your hosted API with their sample dataset, measuring median latency, p95, throughput, and JSON output accuracy. Then if results require, we can run a Dedicated config with reserved GPU pools to measure cost/throughput tradeoff.
[03:18] Ben: What metrics do you capture out of the box?
[03:22] Diego: Token-level latency, per-request end-to-end latency, queueing time, and model variant used. We also surface cost estimates per request and KV-cache hit rates when using prefix caching.
[03:33] Sofia: About KV cache — we use pretty long context windows for some flows, how does caching interact?
[03:39] Diego: We have prefix/KV caching that stores repeated context chunks; in practice it reduces per-token compute and latency when prompts share contexts. We'll include recommended caching config for your templates.
[03:52] Amira: Timeline expectation? We want a decision in 6 weeks.
[03:56] Nora: Proposed POC timeline: Week 0 (this week) — agreement and SOW; Week 1 — integration and baseline runs; Week 2 — benchmark sweep and analysis; Week 3-4 — iterate on prompt engineering and structured-output tuning; Week 5 — pilot load test; Week 6 — final review and decision. Does that align?
[04:17] Ben: Yes, sounds fine.
[04:20] Sofia: We'll need to review SAML and KMS integration early so infra can unblock.
[04:24] Nora: We'll attach the security brief and KMS playbook with the proposal.
[04:28] Diego: Quick technical note on OpenAI-compat: the endpoint paths are identical, we map parameter names but have some Redwood-specific flags for cache controls and preferred model variants. Example: POST /v1/chat/completions works, plus x-redwood-prefer: dedicated to hint route preference.
[04:45] Ben: Can you show an example function schema?
[04:48] Diego: Sure, I'll paste later but here's a simple one: {"name":"extract_invoice","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"amount":{"type":"number"},"vendor":{"type":"string"}},"required":["amount","vendor"]}} — we then get a typed JSON back, sometimes the model returns extra fields so we recommend strict validation step.
[05:08] Amira: If the model occasionally outputs malformed JSON, what's the workaround?
[05:12] Diego: Two paths: 1) use function-calling strict schema enforcement which reduces occurrences, and 2) use a lightweight post-parse sanitizer we ship as part of SDK examples. We'll include those snippets.
[05:25] Nora: On pricing: we'll provide hosted per-token and an estimate for a dedicated reserved instance (monthly) based on your expected throughput. We can show sensitivity to batch sizes and quantization options to hit your cost target.
[05:37] Ben: Are quantized model variants available on the Hosted plan?
[05:40] Diego: Yes, we have quantized variants for many models; performance varies by hardware, we'll document recommended model/quantization combos for your workload.
[05:49] Sofia: For the security review, we might want a short SRE call to walk through VPC peering or private deployment options.
[05:56] Nora: Happy to coordinate. We'll propose a security review slot after you get the security docs.
[06:02] Amira: One more thing — we use existing OpenAI-compatible webhooks; can Redwood forward webhooks or do we need to poll?
[06:09] Diego: We support webhooks for completion events and for audit logs. For low-latency flows we recommend streaming + socket ingestion, but webhooks work for async pipelines.
[06:20] Ben: For the benchmark dataset, we'll provide 1k representative queries plus expected JSON ground truth and evaluation script.
[06:27] Nora: Perfect. We'll run the benchmark, share raw traces, and a summary dashboard.
[06:33] Amira: Ok let's recap next steps.
[06:36] Nora: Recap: Nora to send POC SOW and pricing; Diego to send SDK snippets, function-calling and JSON sanitation examples; Lyra to send prompts and sample dataset; Sofia to send infra requirements; schedule benchmark and security review.
[06:52] Ben: Great, thanks everyone.
[06:55] Amira: Thanks, bye.
[06:57] Nora: Thanks all. We'll follow up via email with links to docs and the SOW.
[07:03] [call end]
